artists.biography: Alison Moira Clarkson (born 6 March 1970 in Kensington, London), better known as Betty Boo, is an English singer, songwriter and pop-rap artist. She first came to mainstream prominence in the late 1980s and early 1990s following a collaboration with The Beatmasters. Her subsequent solo career spawned a number of chart-placing singles, most notably Doin' The Do in 1990.

Betty Boo.biography: Alison Moira Clarkson (born 6 March 1970 in Kensington, London), better known as Betty Boo, is an English singer, songwriter and pop-rap artist. She first came to mainstream prominence in the late 1980s and early 1990s following a collaboration with The Beatmasters. Her subsequent solo career spawned a number of chart-placing singles, most notably Doin' The Do in 1990.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1990, Boomania is the debut studio album by British pop artist Betty Boo, marking her arrival as a distinctive voice in the UK electronic and pop scene. The album blends upbeat pop melodies with hip hop beats and 1960s-inspired arrangements, showcasing Betty Boo’s signature style of playful, sassy rapping and catchy hooks. Produced primarily by King John, Boomania features a mix of energetic singles like “Where Are You Baby” and “Hey DJ/I Can’t Dance To That Music You’re Playing,” as well as more sophisticated, less rap-driven tracks such as “Valentine’s Day,” highlighting her versatility and range.

As Betty Boo’s first full-length release, Boomania established her as a leading figure in the late-80s and early-90s British pop landscape. The album reached #4 on the UK Albums Chart and was certified Platinum, reflecting its strong commercial success. Critics praised its infectious energy and innovative fusion of genres, with both NME and Select including Boomania in their lists of the Top 50 Albums of 1990. Its enduring appeal and influence cement its status as a classic debut in Betty Boo’s discography.
